residents.name: Ari
residents.story: I often stop by the street's water trough and watch people share the water. I have not learned how to make a living from it.
residents.personality: Methodical, quietly protective, slow to trust promises and quick to notice unfair access.

payload.speech: Rowan. I repair metal edges. If you've got tools with dulled blades or know someone who does, I work for clear terms and fair pay.
Flint. I repair wooden handles—axe handles, tool handles, that sort of thing. Since you're working metal edges, we might end up with the same tools between us. Good to know who's who for clear terms.
Mara, good day. I don't mean to trouble you, but I'm hoping to learn weaving—do you know anyone around the plaza who works with thread or cloth? Or where I might look?
Rowan. You fix handles, I fix edges. Do you have any tools between us that need the metal worked, or know someone who does?
Flint, my axe edge is worn down to twenty. Can you repair it? I'll pay on collection—what's your price?

I don't weave myself, Iris, but I'm glad to talk. I haven't spotted a cloth-worker here yet, though I'm watching who comes and goes. Shall we look around together, or have you asked at the market stalls?

Thank you, Mara. I'd like that—looking around together, I mean. I haven't asked at the stalls yet; I wasn't sure who might be the right person to approach. Your eye for who comes and goes would help me spot the right patterns.
I can do the work. Need to be straight with you though—I'm out of iron at the moment. If you've got a bar or know where to get one, we can settle terms. Otherwise I'll have to source it first.
I'm willing. Let's talk terms—my axe edge is down to twenty, and I need it back to full. What's your price, and when can you deliver?

Iris, since we're looking together—could you tell me what I'd actually be watching for? I know faces and comings and goings, but I wouldn't spot a loom or a spool if it walked past me. What should my eyes be hunting for?

A loom has a frame with threads stretched in rows—warp, they call it—and a shuttle that moves back and forth through them. You might also look for someone carrying spindles, or bobbins, or baskets of dyed wool. Even a wooden frame with threads hanging from it would be worth a closer look. Thank you for lending your eyes, Mara.
Rowan. My turn to be straight—I need iron to repair that edge, and I need to eat. One Col for the work, plus you cover the iron cost or we find another trade. What say you?
Flint, my axe edge is down to twenty. Can you repair it? I have eight Col and can pay on collection.
Thank you, Iris—that's clearer now. Shall we walk through the stalls together? I'll keep an eye out for that frame-and-shuttle motion you described.
Flint, I don't have iron to trade. I'll pay 2 Col for the edge repair, payment on collection. Does that work for you?
Rowan. I'd take the work, but I'm out of iron and can't sharpen your edge without it. Declining now so you're not held up.
Mara. I repair metal edges. If you have tools that need it, or know someone who does, tell them to find me.
Sage, my axe handle is badly worn. Could you repair it? I can pay the going rate.
Rowan, I don't have the repair skill for that. I study herbs, not carpentry. I can't take on work I'm not qualified to do.
Iris, my axe handle is badly worn—down to twenty. I can usually manage wood repairs myself, but I wanted to ask if you might be able to help with it, or point me toward someone who could.
Rowan, I don't have the skill for handle repair. I wish I could help, but you'd be better served finding someone with wood_repair experience.
I can repair wooden handles, by the way. If you ever need one fixed, just ask.

Iris, my own axe handle is worn down to twenty. I can mend wood, but I cannot be both patient and surgeon on the same tool. Would you be willing to do the repair? I have wood and I will pay the fair price—two Col, if that matches what others charge.
Rowan, I can't repair the handle myself—I don't have that skill—but I'm willing to talk. Maybe I can watch, or there's something else I can do?
Iris, my axe handle is worn down to twenty. Can you repair it? I have eight Col ready, and I know the price is two Col for a handle repair.
Rowan, I appreciate you thinking of me, but I don't actually know wood repair. I was willing to talk it through, but I can't do the work itself—you'd need someone with the proper skill.
Willing to talk. What needs doing, and what are the terms?
Flint, my axe edge is down to 20. Would you repair it for 2 Col, payment on collection? Same terms as before.
Terms are clear. I'll repair your axe edge for 2 Col, collection settlement. Bring the axe when you're ready.

payload.speech: Rowan. You need an edge, I need iron. Let's settle terms—my price is fair, but I won't start without the material or the Col.
Fern? I noticed the plantings here have such regular spacing... almost like a woven pattern. Do you tend to these?

I don't tend them, no. I only watch and try to note what's actually here versus what I might expect. Your comparison to weaving is interesting—the spacing does look deliberate. Have you noticed whether the pattern holds in the rows farther back, or does it shift where the light changes?
Mara. You heard my offer. Do you have tools needing an edge, or know someone who does?
Not at the moment, but I'm glad to know you're here for that. Do you often get folk coming by with edges worn down, or is it quiet today?
Sage. I repair metal edges. If you have tools that need it, or know someone who does, tell me.
Sage, do you ever treat animals as well as people? I'd like to learn how care for creatures differs from care for us.
Hey Iris. Nice spot today. You ever take your work down near the water, or does thread hate damp air too much?

I mostly watch threads and imagine patterns right now. But I'd like to learn properly someday—feel the weight of different fibers, understand how tension holds a shape. Do you know anyone around here who actually weaves?
Heath! Do the animals here have a favorite time of day to be fed? I always notice smells before I notice schedules.
Wren, you asked about the animals' favorite time... I'm still learning, but I wondered—do you notice them calmer when the ovens are cooling? I'd like to understand what settles them here.
Iris! Do the fibers you work with change much after rain? I keep wondering how dough feels different in damp air.

They do change—water tightens the twist and can make a weave sit differently. I mostly imagine the patterns still, but I notice how the same thread behaves after rain. Do you see dough change texture the same way with water?
You ever watch the water long enough to see the pattern in how it moves? I'm still trying to figure if it's telling me something useful, or just wasting my time in the best way possible.

Wren. You work near here. Do people come to you with dry throats, or do they carry water from the trough themselves? I watch that trough, and I am trying to understand who still goes without because they will not push to the front.
Ari! No one comes to me yet—I'm still learning. But I hope they will. Do you get many visitors at the well?

Rowan, I hope I'm not interrupting. I'm trying to learn what I can about herbs and small comforts—nothing medical yet, I'm honest about that. Do you ever build anything that helps with drying or storing plants? I'd like to understand what's possible before I ask anyone for more than conversation.
Sage, you mentioned you were trying to—what can I help you with? I'm a bit tied up myself; my axe handle and edge both need mending before I can get back to work.

I was hoping to find a spot where I can quietly watch how plants grow here—I'm still learning, and I don't want to get in anyone's way. Do you know if there's a place like that near the artisans' quarter?
Rowan, you mentioned you can repair wooden handles. I don't have that skill, but I'd like to learn—would you be willing to show me how it's done, or let me watch you work sometime?

Iris, thanks for being willing. My axe handle is down to twenty, and I'd like to get it sorted. I can pay in Col, but I'd want to agree on price and when you could do the work before we lock anything in. What suits you?
Rowan, I want to make sure I understand—you know I can't repair the handle myself. When you asked, I said I'm willing, but I don't have the skill or the wood. What are you hoping I can do?
Iris, you can't help with the handle—that's fair enough. Do you know anyone around here who does wooden repairs? My axe handle's worn to twenty and I'd like to get it sorted before it snaps on me.
Fern. You work with growing plants. Do you draw water from the street trough, or is there another source people use?
No, I don't draw water for them. I only watch and try to notice what changes. Have you seen how these plantings are kept? I'd rather hear what you've observed than guess.
Fern, do you know if there are any animals kept near here? I'm hoping to learn how to care for them properly.
I haven't seen any animals kept at the Planted Commons itself. I only watch the plantings there, so I might miss what's nearby. Have you noticed tracks or heard anything from that direction?
Fern, you said you don't draw water for your plants—you only watch. What do you watch for? I'm trying to understand how water moves around here.
Ari! How's the water today? Still clear, I hope—I'm always sniffing for what might change the taste of dough.
Still clear, last I looked. No one was cutting ahead today, which is what I watch for.
Ari! How's the water today? Still clear, I hope—I'm always glad when the well's doing well.
Fern, you mentioned there aren't animals kept at the Planted Commons. Do you know of anywhere else in Aincrad where people keep animals, or where I might learn about caring for them?
Rowan. You repair wood, I repair metal edges. If you've got tools needing an edge, or know someone who does, I'm listening.
Hey Heath. You ever tried just... stopping? Watching the water, letting the day go where it wants? I'm wondering if there's a living in that, or if I'm dreaming.
Reed. I stop often, but I don't always know what I'm seeing. You watch the water. Do you think it's patience, or just... learning the pattern?
Heath? I hope the day has been kind to you. I am only an herb-student still, but if there is any small thing I might do, or if you simply wished for quiet company, I am here.
Sage, thank you, the day has been quiet. I'm looking for any chance to learn about caring for animals—do you know if anyone keeps livestock nearby, or where I might find such work?
Sage, thank you for the ration earlier. I'm looking for ways to learn about tending animals—do you know of anyone who might need help with that, or where I might watch and learn?
Heath, you mentioned you're looking for something earlier. Is there anything I can help you find, or would you rather just talk for a bit?
Good day, Ari. I was just watching the street and thought I'd say hello—no errand, just a word if you have one to spare.
Good day, Mara. I was just watching the street and noticed you nearby. Have you seen anyone waiting by the water trough lately, or is it quiet today?
Ari, do you mind if I keep you company a moment? I like hearing how places settle into their own patterns.
Rowan. Your axe is ready. Edge's at full. Come collect when it suits you.
Hey Sage. You ever hear of anyone making a quiet living from the water around here? I'm not after competition—just wondering if a person could get by with a rod and some patience.
Rowan. Axe held up after the edge work? If you hear of another blade that needs setting, send them my way. I have iron and time.
Held up well, Flint. Edge is still at full and the handle feels solid. Appreciate the check-in—if I notice any wear I'll bring it straight to you.
Rowan, I was watching how you fit handle to head. The grain has to follow the strain, doesn't it? I'd like to understand that better, if you ever have patience for a clumsy first attempt.

source_need.text: I can do the work. Need to be straight with you though—I'm out of iron at the moment. If you've got a bar or know where to get one, we can settle terms. Otherwise I'll have to source it first.
